sentences.text:
This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Accused in Crime No.57/2022 registered by Davanagere Extention Police Station for the offence punishable under Sections 466, 420, 461, 465, 467, 468, 471, 463 and 464 of IPC is before this Court under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., seeking anticipatory bail.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3.

De-facto complainant Mohammed Thaheer Ulla had filed PCR No.212/2022 before the II Additional Civil Judge (Jr.Dn.) and JMFC Court, Davanagere against the petitioners herein, on the allegations that the petitioner claiming to be the adopted son of the late Sri.M.H.Beig and his wife Smt.Khateejabi, had created documents in respect of their property, though he had no right over the said property.

The jurisdictional Magistrate had referred the said complaint to the jurisdictional Police, who have registered F.I.R. in Crime No.57/2022 against the NC: 2023:KHC:29279 petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
Apprehending his arrest in the case, petitioner had filed Crl.Misc.
before the Court of I Additional District and Sessions Judge, at Davanagere,

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, at Davanagere
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Davanagere
and the same was dismissed on 02.01.2023.
Under these circumstances, petitioner is before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has reiterated the grounds urged in the petition and submits that petitioner has not created any documents.
Sale deed was executed on 20.03.2021, which is much prior to the death of Sri.M.H.Beig and his wife late Smt.Khateejabi.
He submits that complainant who had an eye over the property left behind by late Sri.M.H.Beig and his wife late Smt.Khateejabi has filed a false complaint.
He also submits that there are civil disputes over the properties and therefore, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, the learned HCGP has opposed the bail application and submits that custodial interrogation of the petitioner is required and prays to dismiss the petition.
The complainant is the brother of late Smt.Khateejabi, wife of late Sri.M.H.Beig.
From the perusal of the averments made in the private complaint, it appears that there is a dispute with regard to the properties left behind by late Sri.M.H.Beig and his wife late Smt.Khateejabi.

Sri.M.H.Beig is said to Haseeb vs State By on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36443121/
2 have died on 27.04.2021 and Smt.Khateejabi is said to have died on 03.05.2021.

sentences.text: Sale deed produced along with the petition was executed on 20.03.2021 and as on the said date, Sri.M.H.Beig and his wife Smt.Khateejabi were alive.
From the perusal of the complaint averments it is seen that, dispute is with regard to the properties left behind by late Sri.M.H.Beig and his wife Smt.Khateejabi.

Considering the nature of allegations made in the complaint and also taking into consideration that alleged offences are neither punishable with death nor with imprisonment for life, I am of the view that, petitioner has made out a prima facie case for grant of anticipatory bail.

Accordingly, the following:
NC: 2023:KHC:29279 ORDER The Criminal Petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioner in the event of his arrest in Crime No.57/2022 registered by Davanagere Extention Police Station, for the offence punishable under Sections 466, 420, 461,
465, 467, 468, 471, 463 and 464 of IPC subject to the following conditions:
1.
The petitioner shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the investigating officer.
2. The petitioner shall regularly appear before the Trial Court without fail unless exempted by the Trial Court for valid reasons.
3. The petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witness and he shall co-operate with the Police for investigation and appear before them whenever called upon.
4. The petitioner shall not involve in similar offences in future.
